messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Multiple ILB control-plane errors detected for Private VPCs across regions. Initial spike started at 1973500000. Source: GCP internal load-balancer control plane (route propagation failures). Paging oncall now. :rotating_light:

oncall: I'm on it. Acknowledge and pulling logs. Starting timeline in thread.

maya: seeing 502/503 anomalies from our regional ILBs and a sudden drop in cross-region connections. Some backend hits still succeed locally.

liam: grabbing GCP console -> ILB logs. Also seeing a high rate of "route translation" errors in the controlplane stack. Link: https://status.cloud.google.com/ (GCP networking shows partial degradation)

samir: quick check: are Dedicated and Hosted customers affected or just Private VPC?

maya: appears limited to Private VPCs using cross-region ILB fanout. Dedicated hosted endpoints (public) unaffected.

eng-plat: confirmed. Control-plane is delaying route propagation between regions for internal LBs. Some connections get routed to stale backends causing 502s.

liam: pasting relevant log lines from ILB controlplane:
```
2026-03-15T17:05:12Z ERROR route-propagation handleError: failed to sync routes: apis-gcp: translate failed status=RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED
2026-03-15T17:05:13Z WARN fanout: drop request region=eu seq=1123 reason=route-not-found
```

oncall: paging product-ops and cs for customer impact. @product-ops please prepare a short note we can send to affected customers.

product-ops: on it. Asking CS for an initial list of impacted accounts and whether any paid Dedicated contracts are in the group.

cs: pulling list now. Preliminary: 7 Private VPC customers are showing increased error rates in EU->US cross-region calls, and 2 have active production traffic spikes.

maye (sic) — typo correction: maya: update: one customer reported user-facing errors in EU region with request ids starting with "r-9f3".

liam: mitigation options I'm evaluating: 1) Force re-propagation via route refresh API (risky), 2) Shift affected VPCs to regional-only ILB endpoints (manual failover), 3) Apply traffic steering to avoid cross-region paths.

eng-plat: suggest option 2 as safest short-term: create regional ILB listeners and update route targets to avoid the control-plane fanout path. That avoids the buggy propagation path until GCP stabilizes.

samir: can we script the regional failover? If we have to do this for 7 customers manual is slow.

liam: I'm testing a small script now. Example snippet:
```bash
# create a regional backend service and point VPC route to it
gcloud compute backend-services create redwood-regional-bsvc --region=eu-west1 \
  --protocol=TCP --health-checks=ilb-hc-eu
# update target pool and forwarding rules
```

oncall: please be careful with runbook. @eng-plat do we have a documented rollback if the regional service misconfigures?

eng-plat: yes, runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gcp-ilb-failover (follow steps 3-7 for cutover and rollback). Keep windows small and verify health-check pass counts.

liam: testing on staging tenant now. So far cutover succeeds and traffic is stable for the test group. No degraded latency.

maria — wait wrong name, keep participants consistent: maya: noticed increased Cloud NAT errors at the same timestamps; could be related to control-plane backoff causing control channel saturation.

samir: good catch — we should also throttle any periodic route refresh tasks from our side to reduce noise.

oncall: throttling scheduled route-sync jobs across Private VPCs now: `systemctl stop redwood-route-sync` on fleet agents, using deploy-bot to coordinate.

deploy-bot: deploy job queued: stop-route-syncs @fleet (rolling) — started.

liam: staging cutover validated. Begin regional failover for the two highest-impact customers (EU-prod1, EU-prod2). Will update thread per customer.

product-ops: drafting a customer message: short note saying we are investigating an external GCP networking issue causing internal load balancer cross-region failures; mitigation in progress; ETA unknown. Will send once CS approves. :pray:

cs: holding for the cutover confirmation for EU-prod1 before sending.

liam: EU-prod1 cutover completed at 1973501200. Health checks passed 3/3. Error rate dropped to baseline.

cs: EU-prod1 confirmed recovery from their side. They reported restored user flows. Customer comms ready to send.

maria (ignore) — keep channel names consistent: maya: EU-prod2 cutover in progress. Will post logs.

liam: EU-prod2 cutover completed at 1973502000. Some failover noise but stabilized.

eng-plat: recommended next steps: 1) keep regional endpoints for affected customers until GCP confirms fix, 2) throttle route-sync and refresh tasks for Private VPC fleet, 3) open a ticket with GCP for control-plane resource exhaustion with our logs attached.

oncall: creating support ticket with GCP now. Ticket ID: GCP-INC-82419 (internal). Attached logs and timeline.

liam: added note to ticket: observed RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED in route-translation module, and rapid requeue of route updates from multiple VPC agents.

product-ops: pushing customer note now for the 2 impacted high-priority customers. Copy: "We observed cross-region internal LB disruptions tied to GCP networking. We've performed a regional failover for your endpoints which should restore service. We're monitoring and will follow up when the provider confirms a full fix."

cs: sent, customers acknowledged and asked for post-incident RCA.

samir: for long-term: propose adding a routing polyfill in our runtime to detect stale ILB routes and prefer local-region backends automatically. Also consider rate-limiting our route pushes when we see control-plane errors.

eng-plat: agree. Add to roadmap and create a follow-up ticket to design automatic regional fallback.

oncall: handing to night oncall (maya) for monitoring and follow-up. If GCP provides an update or ticket moves, ping this thread and escalate to SRE leads.

maya: ack. I'll keep watch and coordinate with GCP. Setting daily checks for the ticket and route propagation metrics.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigation performed (regional failovers for 2 high-impact customers, throttle of route-sync jobs). 5 additional Private VPCs remain on monitoring with reduced traffic via throttle. Ticket GCP-INC-82419 opened.

liam: final notes for the handoff: logs + scripts used are in the incident folder `gs://redwood-incident-logs/1973500000/`. Runbook edits pending to add a quick failover script.

product-ops: capturing postmortem template and will schedule an internal post-incident review with eng-plat, SRE, and CS.

cs: customers requesting ETA for full provider fix — we don't have one. Will update when GCP responds.

oncall: closing active paging. Leave thread open for follow-ups and RCA drafts. Thanks team :heart:
